name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping

1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

prose.intro_html:
Street corn is one of those things that tastes like a splurge and cooks like a weeknight. We took elote off the cob, folded it into a creamy salad, and set it over cilantro lime rice with seasoned chicken. The result eats like a food truck order and prices out like a home cook who actually reads the receipt.

Here is the honest math. Every container lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, which clears our 40 gram floor and stays well under the 800 ceiling. That is a real dinner, not a sad diet plate.
prose.shop_smart:
• Chicken breast is the anchor at 4 3/4 pounds, so grab a family pack and cover the whole batch in one purchase. You are cutting every piece into 1-inch chunks, so do not fuss over how the tray looks.
  • Canned corn is the practical move. You need 7 cups drained, so a few standard cans hit the mark and skip off-season cob prices.
  • Long grain white rice is your carbohydrate, and 3 1/2 cups uncooked is a small ask from a big bag. Buy the large bag and the rest keeps for months.
  • Limes pull triple duty here, in the rice, in the corn salad, and as the finish. Grab a full net bag so you are never rationing zest.
  • Cotija shows up in the salad and again on top. One block covers both jobs, and any firm crumbly cheese fills in if the shelf is bare.
prose.make_it:
This is a four-part build that comes together in about 45 minutes total. Nothing here is hard. It is a rice pot, a mixing bowl, and a skillet working in sequence.

  1. Cilantro lime rice. Bring your water to a boil, then add the 3 1/2 cups of rice and the sea salt. Cover, drop the heat to low, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Fold the chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice, and lime zest into the warm rice and set it aside.
  2. Street corn salad. In a large bowl combine the corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, cilantro, and the salt. Stir gently, taste, and adjust. Set it aside to let the flavors meet.
  3. Season the chicken. Mix the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and sea salt in a small bowl. Toss the chicken chunks in the blend until every piece is coated.
  4. Cook the chicken. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the chicken and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it is cooked through and the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees.
  5. Assemble. Lay a bed of cilantro lime rice in each container. Top with chicken, a generous scoop of street corn, cubed avocado, sliced red onion, a shower of cilantro, a sprinkle of cotija, and a squeeze of lime.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers, and the honest way to split it is by weight, not by eyeball. Weigh the full pot of rice, the bowl of corn salad, and the cooked chicken, then divide each total by 14. Now you know exactly how much of each goes in every box, and nobody gets shorted.

Build them in order. Rice as the base, then an even share of chicken, then a scoop of corn salad, and finish with avocado, red onion, cilantro, and cotija. The toppings are meant to stretch across all 14, so go light on the first few and you will not run dry on the last.

steps: Cook the rice in boiling salted water, covered on low, about 20 minutes until tender, then fold in chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice, and lime zest.
Make the street corn salad by combining corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, optional diced jalapeno, cilantro, and salt; stir gently and set aside.
Season the chicken chunks with a blend of chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and sea salt.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium and cook the chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side until it reaches 165 degrees.
Assemble each container with cilantro lime rice, chicken, a scoop of street corn, avocado, red onion, cilantro, cotija, and a squeeze of lime.
